confirmed.title: Lobsters comment threads: each comment becomes an AI one-line 'headline' cut at 200 characters, its text is deleted, and its title links to /login or to a URL quoted in it
confirmed.where: src/content/extract/generic.ts:340-358 (Out.rewriteIfLong) with toItem's title fallback at generic.ts:2960 and 2977 (textLines first line, cut to 197+…)
confirmed.evidence: Harness on live https://lobste.rs/s/olnqh2/websites_should_be_printable (and the same HTML replayed offline): the comments are 'items [oneliner] ai=news'. The first comment is 2679 characters on the page. Sift's item title is the first 197 characters + '…'. The item has no text and no body, and its closing sentence ('very easy to cause trouble with them') appears 0 times in the outline. The 'I... don't even have a printer' comment links to /login (the upvote arrow a.upvoter href=/login, text '~'). The first comment links to /TR/using-aria/#rule1, a URL quoted inside it. A comment also gets the meta '6 comments'. The replies that round 9 now nests under each comment have the same form. pre-round-9 (p9m.js) gives the same items, so this is not a regression. Not checked in the real extension, to avoid AI line calls. It runs the same extract().
confirmed.repro: cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9 && bun run.ts r10m.js,p9m.js https://lobste.rs/s/olnqh2/websites_should_be_printable 1 --wait 2500 | grep -n 'items\|^  \*' ; offline: bun run.ts r10m.js /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r10/dl/lob.html 1 --as https://lobste.rs/s/olnqh2/websites_should_be_printable
confirmed.suspectedCause: Lobsters comments have no heading, and div.comment_text matches no POST_BODY. So toItem names each comment by its first text line (cut at 200) and takes a link inside it (the upvoter or a quoted URL) as its target. Out.rewriteIfLong then sees 4 or more entries averaging over 13 title words, marks the block oneliner/news, moves each entry's text into AI context, and sets it.text = undefined. Lead: never rewrite entries whose title came from textLines (not a heading or a naming link), or entries in a comments area. Treat comment_text/comment-body/comment-content as the post body, and never take a vote link as an entry's target.
confirmed.verdict: I reproduced the outcome, but the claimed cause is wrong. I ran a bundle built fresh from sift-test-8 src on live https://lobste.rs/s/olnqh2/websites_should_be_printable. The comment block is 'items [oneliner] ai=news'. The first comment's title is 198 characters (197 plus the ellipsis). It has text=undefined, context=undefined and no body, so roughly 2,400 characters of that comment never show. Replies have the same form. Titles link to /login, or to a URL quoted in the comment (w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1). p9m.js gives the same result, so this is not a regression. Real cause, found with instrumentation: Lobsters marks every comment's text as <div role="heading" aria-level="3" class="comment_text">. toItem therefore takes the whole comment as the heading: title = textIn(heading), cut at 197. The text walk then skips every text node with 'heading?.contains(own) continue' (48 nodes skipped for the first comment). The text is never collected, so rewriteIfLong does not delete it, and textLines is not used. ctx.inComments is false here. When the heading has no link, the named-link fallback picks the upvoter arrow (a.upvoter, href=/login, text '~' or '31') as main. rewriteIfLong then marks the top-level list as oneliner/news, so each top-level comment's 197 characters are replaced by an AI headline. Nested replies (it.replies) render without rewrite and keep the cut title. This is a real loss of content on a major discussion site, so high or medium severity. The site's ARIA misuse does not excuse Sift, because the spec says Sift works on any site.
confirmed.fix:
In generic.ts toItem, around line 2907, do not accept a [role=heading] that is not h1-h6 as the entry's heading when it holds block content (more than one

, a

    , or text over about 200 characters). Treat it as the post body instead, so bodyEl/postBodyOf reads the comment in full. Also treat .comment_text as a POST_BODY so the comments area is detected (ctx.inComments). In the named-link filter around line 2928, exclude voteLink(a) so an upvote arrow is never main. In Out.rewriteIfLong (line 342), skip blocks whose entries have a body, or whose title came from a heading that holds paragraphs.

confirmed.title: Pages without a lang attribute get a wrong guessed language: Dutch is marked 'en', Catalan 'es', and that wrong language goes to Sift's lang attribute, its UI and the AI lines
confirmed.where: src/content/dom.ts:895-927 (LANG_WORDS, textLang, the pick at 920), via lang() at 886 and generic.ts:7889
confirmed.evidence: Harness on a Dutch news list with no lang (fx/r10rev-nl-nolang.html): page.lang = 'en'. Before round 9 it was ''. Catalan (fx/r10rev-ca-nolang.html): 'es' (was ''). Swedish: ''. Real extension on the Dutch fixture: Sift's .sift div has lang='en' (html lang '', navigator en-US). Screen readers then read the Dutch text with the English voice, and setLang('en') picks Sift's English table although Sift has an nl table. In src/background/index.ts:507-514, a known page language forces every list line into that language for every mode except news. So a Dutch store or video list without lang would get English lines; before, each title's language was detected.
confirmed.repro: cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9 && bun run.ts r10m.js,p9m.js http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r10rev-nl-nolang.html 1 | grep source= ; same for r10rev-ca-nolang.html; real: SIFT_PORT=9468 SIFT_TAB=R1-extractor bun scripts/act.ts goto:http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r10rev-nl-nolang.html wait:6000 "eval:document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('.sift').getAttribute('lang')"
confirmed.suspectedCause: Only 6 languages are scored, and the lead test (12 or more hits, 1.5 times the runner-up) never checks that the winner explains much of the text. Dutch 'is/in/was' count as English, and Catalan 'el/del/una/al' (plus 'les' and 'per' spread over fr and it) count as Spanish. Lead: require that the winner's words are a real share of all words, add stop words that rule a language out (nl: de het een van; ca: els amb però), or use chrome.i18n.detectLanguage. Keep '' when unsure.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. Harness on the fixtures: Dutch gives lang=en (p9m.js gives ''), and Catalan gives es (p9m.js gives ''). To rule out fixtures built to hit the word lists, I ran real pages with the lang attribute and the content-language meta removed. nos.nl gives 'en'. ara.cat and vilaweb.cat both give 'es'. p9m.js gives '' on all three. nl and ca Wikipedia gave '' with both bundles. In the real extension on the Dutch fixture, the .sift element has lang='en' (the html lang is '', navigator is en-US). So Sift marks Dutch text as English for screen readers. From reading the code, not observed: background/index.ts:507-508 forces every non-news list line into the known page language, so a lang-less Dutch store or video list would get English lines. The Short version prompt says 'same language as the text', so articles are not affected. This only hits pages without lang, but those are exactly the pages textLang exists for, and the guess is wrong for two major languages.
confirmed.fix: In dom.ts textLang (lines 895-927), require the winner's hits to be a real share of all words (for example at least 6-8%). Add stop words that rule a language out (nl: de het een van niet op; ca: els amb però dels per a la) or score nl and ca as their own languages. Alternatively use chrome.i18n.detectLanguage with its isReliable flag. Return '' when unsure.

Lead: in toItem, skip a 'Copy link' button when the entry has its own target (main). Keep it on app pages and in dialogs (F904's shared-folder case).
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. In the harness on live theverge.com there are 17 'Copy link' actions now and 0 with p9m.js. In the real extension on port 9468, Sift's view has 17 Copy link buttons, all inside li.item entries ('X has another new head of product.', 'Today's Vergecast…', 'Proton To Re-Interview…'). confirmed.title: The Mirror: headline links, Sign in and 'Open image' do nothing in Sift, with no explanation; the site blocks clicks until a privacy choice that Sift hides
confirmed.evidence: On the home page, act.ts click on 'Storms Boelo and Austen…', 'Harry Kane beats…' and Enter on 'Bank bosses…' (each an <a> with the right href, e.g. …/flood-warnings-alerts-boelo-austen-37811134) left the URL at https://www.mirror.co.uk/ after 7-12 s. On the article, 'User Avatar - redirects to sign in and sign up' and 'Open image' also did nothing (no navigation, no dialog). Menu does work. With Sift off, the original shows a full-page 'We value your privacy' wall (More Options / Reject and Pay / I Accept) over the page. An in-page a.click() on the original anchor (Sift off, body not inert) did not navigate and never reached a click listener on the anchor. So the site swallows clicks until the choice is made. Sift hides that wall and gives no word about it. On the Guardian, Sift explains the same situation ('The site asks for a cookie choice before it plays this video'). A Sift reader on the Mirror has dead headlines. I did not accept the wall, so I could not see the original's behavior after a choice. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r10t2-mirror-orig-avatar.png (original with the wall), /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r10t2-mirror-art.png
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/act.ts goto:https://www.mirror.co.uk/ wait:8000 click:"Harry Kane beats" wait:10000 url  → prints https://www.mirror.co.uk/ (no navigation). Then press:Alt+Shift+S to see the original's privacy wall.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The consent manager (Reach / Quantcast qc-cmp2) blocks clicks in the capture phase while consent is pending. Sift replays the click on the original element, where it is swallowed. Sift's consent explanation (F826) seems to run only for video Play, not for links or buttons that a pending consent blocks.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on the Mirror home page in Sift. act.ts clicks on 'Harry Kane beats…' and 'Bank bosses…' left the URL at https://www.mirror.co.uk/ after 10 s. On the article, 'Open image' also did nothing: no navigation and no Sift layer. I switched to the original and saw the full-page InMobi/Quantcast 'We value your privacy' wall (screenshot: research/shots/skeptic-mirror-orig.png). I dispatched a click on the original anchor with Sift off and traced it. The InMobi CMP's document capture-phase listener (cmp.inmobi.com/tcfv2/61/cmp2ui-en.js) calls preventDefault and stopImmediatePropagation on the click, so the anchor never gets it. Sift's outline has no privacy, cookie or consent text. A new Sift reader on the Mirror gets dead links and buttons, with no hint that a choice is pending and no way to make it inside Sift. The only consent explanation (F826, consentFirst) runs on video Play.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/index.ts H.act (around proxy.click(el) near line 3315), check after the replayed click whether it was default-prevented and whether consentWallUp() returns a wall. If so, show that wall the way the Play path does (askConsent(true) and consentKey, near lines 1901-1935), with a new i18n line such as 'The site asks for a cookie choice before it opens links'. In generic.ts, the consent-why block (around line 6807) should then also cover links and buttons. Do not navigate around the wall.

confirmed.title: G1 article Short version is written in English on a Portuguese page, and the English version is cached
confirmed.evidence: The page is html lang pt-BR, and Sift's view has lang pt-BR with Portuguese UI. The Short version paragraphs read 'Trump said Brazil’s election looked fraudulent but gave no evidence. He also said he likes Lula.', 'Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro, a Trump ally, in the presidential runoff…' and so on. The cache entry (02:37:30, 1544 chars) holds the English text, and its saved input text is Portuguese ('Sem apresentar provas, Trump fala de…'). A second visit about an hour later showed the same English text. Round 9 saw this article's Short version in Portuguese ('Trump afirmou, sem provas, que a eleição brasileira “pareceu fraudada”…', /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9t2/g1trump-short.txt). Spanish Short versions on Infobae, La Nación and Clarín stayed Spanish today. Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r10t2-g1-english-short2.png
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/act.ts goto:<g1 url> wait:20000 'eval:[...document.querySelector("sift-root").shadowRoot.querySelectorAll("p")].map(p=>p.innerText).filter(t=>/^Trump said/.test(t))'  → ['Trump said Brazil’s election looked fraudulent…']. It is cached, so every visit shows it until the entry expires.
confirmed.suspectedCause: doCondense never checks the language of its output. The only language rule is in the prompt ('Same language as the text. Never translate.'), and the user message around the text is English ('Title: … The text has N words. Write about …'). A model that answers in English is saved and shown. A script and language check like vetLine's for lines (scriptFits / entryLang against req.lang) is missing for condense.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on two visits. The G1 page is html lang pt-BR and Sift's root is lang pt-BR. The Short version paragraphs are in English: 'Trump said Brazil’s election looked fraudulent but gave no evidence…', 'Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro, a Trump ally…' and 'Asked if he would act on the result…'. One Portuguese paragraph sits among them. The same English text came back on the second visit, so it is served from cache. In src/background/index.ts, doCondense (lines 738-860) does no language check on the model's output. checked() only strips preambles, title lines and unsupported quotes. The only guard is the prompt rule 'Same language as the text. Never translate.', and the user message around the text is English. Lines get a language check through scriptFits/entryLang (around line 680); condense has none.
confirmed.fix: In src/background/index.ts doCondense, after the model call and before save(), check the language of the output against req.lang. Reuse entryLang/scriptFits/langScript from src/background/text.ts, as the line check does around line 680. On a mismatch, retry once with a note that names the language, and never cache a wrong-language result. Also run that check in checked() on cache hits, so the English entry already cached is dropped. Optionally name the language in the user message ('Write in Portuguese').

confirmed.title: La Nación home headline lines misattribute: Milei's allies become Bolsonaro's, and a quote about the vote extension is pinned on Lula's win
confirmed.where: https://www.lanacion.com.ar/ (home, headline lines after the AI rewrite)
confirmed.evidence: (1) The original card is 'Los amigos de Milei. Tras la derrota de Bolsonaro, las elecciones que ponen a prueba al club de sus aliados'. The article H1 is 'Las elecciones que ponen a prueba al club de aliados internacionales de Milei'. Sift's line says 'Las elecciones que ponen a prueba a los aliados de Bolsonaro tras su derrota'. That names the wrong leader. (2) The original card is '"Hubo un gravísimo error". Diego Guelar analizó el triunfo de Lula: “cambio de reglas”, la relación con Milei y el posible indulto a Bolsonaro'. Sift's line says 'Diego Guelar analizó el triunfo de Lula, un “gravísimo error”, el “cambio de reglas”, …', which reads as if Guelar called Lula's win a grave error. The article says Guelar called the court's two-hour extension of voting a 'gravísimo error'. This is the F927 pattern (a teaser quote joined to the story's event), still alive with PROMPT_VERSION 11. The other 98 La Nación pairs I read are faithful. Pairs: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r10t2/ln-home-pairs.txt
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/act.ts goto:https://www.lanacion.com.ar/ wait:60000 'eval:[...document.querySelector("sift-root").shadowRoot.querySelectorAll("a")].filter(a=>/Guelar|ponen a prueba/.test(a.innerText)).map(a=>a.innerText)'. Then open the two hrefs (…/tras-la-derrota-de-bolsonaro-las-elecciones-que-ponen-a-prueba-al-club-de-aliados-internacionales-de-nid26102026/ and …/diego-guelar-analizo-el-triunfo-de-lula-…-nid25102026/) and read the H1 and the 'gravísimo error' sentence.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The news-line prompt's new rule covers only order and cause words ('after', 'because'). It does not cover resolving a pronoun ('sus aliados') to the nearest name, dropping the kicker that names the subject ('Los amigos de Milei'), or attaching a separate kicker quote by apposition. vetLine's quoteAsFact does not catch a quote moved next to a different noun.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced from the cached lines on La Nación home. (1) Sift shows 'Las elecciones que ponen a prueba a los aliados de Bolsonaro tras su derrota'. The original card reads 'A FONDO Los amigos de Milei. Tras la derrota de Bolsonaro, las elecciones que ponen a prueba al club de sus aliados'. The article H1 (fetched) is 'Las elecciones que ponen a prueba al club de aliados internacionales de Milei'. Sift's line names the wrong leader, a clear factual error. (2) Sift shows 'Diego Guelar analizó el triunfo de Lula, un “gravísimo error”, el “cambio de reglas”…'. The article's kicker is the separate quote '"Hubo un gravísimo error".' The body says Guelar called the court's two-hour voting extension a 'gravísimo error'. Placed right after 'el triunfo de Lula', the quote reads as apposition, as if he called Lula's win the error. Item 1 alone is a high-severity meaning error, and item 2 is misleading.
confirmed.fix: In src/background/index.ts, add to the news-line rules (the news prompt's LINES_RULES section): a kicker before the headline ('Los amigos de Milei.', a quote) sets whose story it is. A possessive ('sus') refers to the kicker's subject, never to the nearest name. A kicker quote stays with its speaker and is never set beside another noun. In vetLine, reject a line that drops a person's name present in the kicker and adds a possessive tie to a different name. Extend quoteAsFact (src/background/text.ts) to flag a title's kicker quote placed directly after a different noun phrase.

confirmed.title: La Nación Claves: the 'El giro político de los gobiernos sudamericanos' maps are lost; only the title, legend and the years show
confirmed.evidence: The original has a 896x867 graphic (div.ln-nd-mapa-gobiernos-latam-nuevo-title, 2 svgs). It shows two maps of South America for 2006 and 2026, with each of ten countries colored Izquierda or Derecha. Sift, in both the Short version and the full text, shows only the lines 'El giro político de los gobiernos sudamericanos', 'La orientación política de diez gobiernos…', 'Izquierda Derecha', '2006', '2026' and the Venezuela footnote. There is no portal or image, and the country names are gone. The reader cannot tell which governments were left or right, which is the point of the graphic. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r10t2-ln-giro-sift.png (Sift), /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r10t2-ln-giro-orig.png (original)
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/act.ts goto:<claves url> wait:20000 'eval:(()=>{const R=document.querySelector("sift-root").shadowRoot;const t=R.querySelector(".sift").innerText;const i=t.indexOf("El giro político");return [t.slice(i,i+250),[...R.querySelectorAll("[aria-label]")].map(e=>e.getAttribute("aria-label")).filter(l=>/giro|gobiernos/i.test(l))]})()'  → loose legend lines and no portal.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The F929 small-chart rule keeps seat charts whose text is labels plus numbers. This map's text is a title, a legend and country names with no numbers, so it falls through to text blocks. The SVG drawing is dropped, and the country labels are dropped as well.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced in both the Short version and 'Ver texto completo'. Sift shows only 'El giro político de los gobiernos sudamericanos', the subtitle, 'Izquierda Derecha', '2006', '2026' and the Venezuela footnote. It has no portal and no image (screenshot: research/shots/skeptic-ln-giro-sift.png). The original div.ln-nd-mapa-gobiernos-latam-nuevo-root (896x867, 2 SVGs) draws two South America maps for 2006 and 2026, each country colored left or right (screenshot: research/shots/skeptic-ln-giro-orig.png). The ten country names are SVG <text>, which Sift drops. The code explains it. dataWidget needs a select or button. dataChart needs at least 3 numeric parts outside the SVG, and chartParts skips SVG text, so only 2006 and 2026 count. The graphic falls through to text blocks, and SKIP drops the svg.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts, widen dataChart (around line 1797) or add a sibling check for a captioned SVG graphic in an article. A box of at least 300x200 holding SVGs with many path/polygon shapes and SVG <text> labels, with only a title, legend and footnote outside, should be kept as a chart portal like F929. Its SVG text labels could also be read into the label so screen readers get the country names.

confirmed.suspectedCause: An inline 'READ MORE:' label followed by a link to another story is kept as article content. A rule that drops in-body 'Read more / READ MORE / Also read' cross-links (as done for related-story boxes) does not catch this Mirror markup.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on two loads. Between the article paragraphs, Sift shows 'READ MORE: New HMRC £1,000 tax alert…' and 'READ MORE: Jamie Oliver's wife says…' as linked paragraphs. Neither is related to the Lula story (screenshot: research/shots/skeptic-mirror-sift-readmore.png). In the original, each is a div.ReadMore_readmore-container holding span[data-testid=readmore] 'READ MORE:' and an <a data-tmdatatrack='read-more'> to another story. These are in-body cross-promos, which the spec says Sift removes. Medium is fair: two noise lines inside the Short version.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts, drop an in-article block whose text is only a 'Read more / READ MORE / Also read / Leer más / Leia também:' label plus one link to another article. Match by text pattern and by class or test-id tokens (readmore, read-more). The check could go in the promo test or the noise token regex in src/content/dom.ts (around line 805), which already lists 'related' and 'promo' but not 'read-?more'.

confirmed.suspectedCause: A lazy image inside a
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on two loads. Sift's view has 1 , the first photo. The second and third photos appear only as links: 'View 3 Images Re-elected President of Brazil…' and 'View 3 Images Federal Deputy Andre Janones…'. In the original, all three are button.SlideViewerButton (604x490) with an . The first is loading=eager, the other two loading=lazy and never loaded (naturalWidth 0, getBoundingClientRect width 0, height 402). photoButton (generic.ts around line 1947) needs img width of at least 160, so the lazy ones fail. They are then handled as a button with the button's text. Their content photos are lost.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts photoButton, measure an unloaded lazy img by its button's or parent's width when its own rect width is 0, or reuse the lazy-size fallback from contentImage (around line 1628). Then figure()/contentImage keep the photo with its src from srcset or src, and the caption becomes the figcaption, not a link label.

rejected.title: pageShowsDate is quadratic on long stories whose JSON-LD date is not shown: about 3x slower extraction on every pass
rejected.where: src/content/extract/generic.ts:7047-7068 (pageShowsDate, gen13 F957), the box test at 7062; called from ldDate at 7031
rejected.evidence:
Harness, fx/r10rev-ld4000.html (4000

in one div.entry-content, each with a year, BlogPosting JSON-LD datePublished 2025-03-14 not shown, no meta date, no ): 2.0-3.8 s per extract(). The same page with one visible 'Ana Ruiz · 14 March 2025' line (fx/r10rev-ld4000-shown.html), where pageShowsDate returns early: 0.6-1.2 s (5 runs each, twice). With pageShowsDate stubbed to 'none' in the current bundle, a 1500-paragraph copy drops from 790-1170 ms to 250-470 ms. Every re-extraction pays it.
rejected.repro: cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9 && bun run.ts r10m.js http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r10rev-ld4000.html 5 --quiet ; bun run.ts r10m.js http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r10rev-ld4000-shown.html 5 --quiet
rejected.suspectedCause: For every text node with a year, (p.parentElement.textContent?.length ?? 0) < 200 builds the grandparent's whole text just to compare its length. When the paragraphs sit in one big content div, that is the whole story for each node: O(nodes × story size). Lead: test the parent's size cheaply (cached tlen, or a childElementCount/child-count guard), or read the parent's text only when p is a small inline element. Cap the nodes scanned.
rejected.verdict: The mechanism is real, but it does not reach medium severity on realistic pages. On the 4000-paragraph fixture I measured about 2.0-2.9 s against 0.63-1.15 s for the -shown copy, in two runs. With only pageShowsDate stubbed to 'none', the same page goes from about 2.0 s to about 0.6 s, and p9m.js runs it in 0.53-0.77 s. So the quadratic cost is pageShowsDate's box test at generic.ts:7062, which reads the whole container's textContent for every text node with a year. The cost is small at realistic sizes. Built from the same fixture: 300 paragraphs, each with a year, gives about 35 ms against 30 ms warm. 1000 paragraphs gives about 180 ms against 100 ms. It needs a page with BlogPosting or NewsArticle JSON-LD, no published_time meta, no meta date and no <time datetime>, that never shows its date in a matching format, with thousands of year-bearing text nodes sitting directly in one container. That is a contrived page, so the claimed '3x slower on every pass' applies only to the synthetic fixture. Cheap hardening would still be worth doing: test the parent's size with the cached tlen() or childElementCount before reading its textContent, and cap the walk.
rejected.fix: Optional hardening in pageShowsDate (generic.ts:7062): use p.parentElement.childElementCount <= 6 && tlen(p.parentElement) < 200 (cached), or only widen the box when p is an inline element. Cap the number of nodes walked (for example 2000).
